summary: End-to-end frontend testing of FlowDine marketing site (React-only, no backend). Verified routing, navigation, modal flows, pricing toggle, blog grid + detail pages, 404 handling, mobile menu, sticky navbar, ScrollToTop, and graceful Web3Forms fallback. 25/25 functional checks passed (3 reported test-script failures were false positives caused by Indian-locale price formatting and a substring overlap; the underlying app behavior is correct).

integration_issues.issue: CORS error to api.web3forms.com (expected — placeholder access key 'YOUR_WEB3FORMS_ACCESS_KEY'). Fallback path correctly fires success toast and closes modal after 2.2s. Behaves as documented intentional UX.

action_items: (Optional) Replace placeholder Web3Forms access key when going live — current key intentionally fails CORS, fallback success state masks real failure.
(Nit) Consider stricter inline field-level validation messages on ContactModal (currently only a toast). Toast disappears quickly and there is no per-field highlight for missing required fields.
critical_code_review_comments: ContactModal.jsx: success-fallback on catch / non-success response means real Web3Forms failures (after key replacement) will silently look successful to the user. After replacing the key, recommend showing actual error toast on real failure instead of a generic success toast.
PricingPage.jsx uses ₹{price.toLocaleString('en-IN')} — good for users, but be aware that this means tests/scrapers will see '1,999' not '1999'.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All testids verified. Public URL: https://order-sync-54.preview.emergentagent.com. Pricing prices render with Indian locale separator (₹999, ₹1,999, ₹2,999) — when asserting use 'in' check carefully or strip commas. Web3Forms key is placeholder; modal always shows success toast via catch-fallback (intentional). All 5 blog slugs verified: why-restaurant-service-is-slow, manual-vs-digital-restaurant-management, best-restaurant-management-software, qr-ordering-benefits, restaurant-analytics-for-profit.
